en: Regarding the training in the *krama-sandhāna* as it has been traditionally handed down at the conclusion of the *krama* sections: the method of joining [the words] according to the rules of the *krama-śāstra* is now being explained.

The all-sustainer with the highest [power] has poured forth the hundred-streamed, the thousand-streamed, the god who is unassailable; she is the all-nourishing one. May this be successful for Indra. I go; who [is there]? For that purpose, O Vāc, you are burnt away. O enemies, wide space! I go; Bhūḥ! We are the destroyers of the gods. The most divine invoker of the gods, the unshakable, the oblation-holder—Viṣṇu, with both hands, I take it for Agni, for the existent. With the rays, O goddesses, you who are devoted to the gods, you belong to Agni.

To Agni and Soma, for the divine [sacrifice] (20); let the pressing-stone know [thee] (21); let [the fire] of Agni know [thee] (22); O *śamī* tree, thou art the preparer of the oblation (23); go, O cock (24); carry [us] firmly (25); for slaughter, O Agni (26); the atmosphere is the support (27); for all [beings], the heaven (28); let the grain know [thee] (29); for the out-breath (*vyāna*), the long [line] (30); rich in sap (31); let them be asked for the sake of procreation (32); O Earth, do not harm (33); O sheep, do not perish (34); may you be bound, O harmless one (35); with the *gāyatra* [meter] (36); with the *jāgata* [meter], the subtle [threads] (37); I wipe [them] with the sharpened [blade] (38).
"I wipe for Aditi" (39), "I see for Agni" (40), "for each Yajus of Savitṛ" (41), "thee, splendor" (42)—thus there are forty-two [verses] in the first chapter.

To the Lord, the Gandharva; 1. Praised by Indra; 2. The right-hand [deities] are Mitra and Varuṇa; 3. For protection from calumny, [the praise] of Savitṛ; 4. Firm, firm; 5. I cleanse with obeisance; 6. May they accompany us; 7. I eat this; 8. To Brahman, by that; 9. I move Agni and Soma; 10. I move for Indra and Agni; 11. Of Indra and Agni, Indra and Agni; 12. Indra and Agni, for the Vasus; 13. May they protect, may they enjoy; 14. Indra with the Maruts; 15. For that nourishment; 16. O Agni, turn back; 17. I have approached the winters; 18. Those who sit upon the altar; 19. Thus nineteen [verses] in the second chapter.

"Ūṣasā sūryyaḥ" (1), "gṛhapate purīṣyaḥ" (2), and "pativedanamitaḥ" (3)—these are the three *krama-sandhānas* in the third chapter (3). In the fourth [chapter], there is an absence of *krama-sandhāna* (4).

"purūravā manthāmi" (1), "rajaḥ śayā hariśayā" (2), "devavītaye siṃhi" (3), "dhruvo vaiṣṇavam" (4), "dhruva aindram" (5), "havvyavāhanaḥ śvātraḥ" (6), and "abhūdyathāyatham" (7)—these are the seven [sections] in the fifth chapter (5).

In the sixth chapter, there is an absence of *krama-sandhāna*: (6) "mādayasva udānāya" (1) and "bhūn mahendrāya" (2)—these two [cases] constitute *krama-sandhāna*. In the seventh chapter, [there is an absence of *krama-sandhāna*].
In the eighth chapter, there is an absence of *krama-sandhāna*: (8).
"Indrasya satyaprasavaḥ" (1) and "Indra vājajit" (2)—these two are *kramasaṃdhāna*s in the ninth chapter (9).
In the tenth chapter, there is an absence of *kramasaṃdhāna* (10).
"Jāgatena haste" (1) and "Hiraṇyayīm ānuṣṭubhena" (2)—these two are *kramasaṃdhāna*s in the eleventh chapter (11).
"paricillokam" (1)—this is one *krama-sandhāna* in the twelfth chapter (12);
"sāhasram" (1), "gavayamūrṇāyutam" (2), "uṣṭramajaḥ" (3), and "śarabhamtvam" (4)—these are four *krama-sandhānas* in the thirteenth chapter (13);
"antarikṣaṃ vāyuḥ" (1), "vāyūrājñī" (2), and "bṛhatī nabhaḥ" (3)—these are three *krama-sandhānas* in the fourteenth chapter (14).

Agniveśa 1, Rathacitra Menakā 2, Asamaratha Pramlocantī 3, Ariṣṭanemi Viśvācī 4, Suṣeṇa Urvaśī 5, the two Śaiśiras Parameṣṭhī 6, Divaḥ Sūrya 7, and Divaṃ Dhruva 8—these are the eight [sections] in the fifteenth chapter.
Chapters sixteen and seventeen are devoid of *krama-sandhāna*. 16, 17.
Svastoma 1 and Rathantara Vveṭ 2—these two are the *krama-sandhānas* in the eighteenth chapter. 18.
In the nineteenth chapter, there is an absence of sequential conjunction (krama-sandhāna).
[The four cases are: 1. Vāyu in the waking state; 2. Sūrya in the dream state; 3. Śūdra and Ārya; 4. Āpaḥ and Ayakṣi. In the twentieth chapter, there are four such sequential conjunctions.
In the twenty-first chapter, there is an absence of sequential conjunction.
"svāhākṛtaḥ svagā" (1), "prāṇāya yatte" (2)—these two [sections] are in the twenty-second chapter (22).
"The moon is four-footed" (1), "the moon is in the night" (2), "Vāyu and Sūrya" (3)—these three are the *kramasandhāna*s in the twenty-third chapter (23).
There is an absence of *kramasandhāna* in the twenty-fourth, twenty-fifth, twenty-sixth, and twenty-seventh chapters (24, 25, 26, 27).

"śucimuṣṇihā" (1) and "devau triṣṭubhā" (2)—these two are *krama-sandhāna*s in the twenty-eighth chapter (28). There is an absence of *krama-sandhāna* in the twenty-ninth (29), thirtieth (30), thirty-first (31), thirty-second (32), thirty-third (33), thirty-fourth (34), and thirty-fifth (35) chapters. "ūtibhiḥ kayā" (1) and "īkṣa'īkṣāmahe" (2)—these two are *krama-sandhāna*s in the thirty-sixth chapter (36).
*pāhi madhu* (1) *svāhā rātriḥ* (2)—these two [are found] in the thirty-seventh chapter (37).
*sarasvatyasau* (1)—this one is in the thirty-eighth chapter (38).
In the thirty-ninth chapter (39), there is an absence of sequential connection (krama-sandhāna).
"Know ignorance, O Āyā! Oṃ 3 Krato! Remember, O Klibe! What was done, O Kilbe! Thus, there are four [mantras] in the fortieth chapter.
There are one hundred and fifteen *krama-sandhānas* in total.
In cases other than these, the determination is made according to the *saṃhitā*.
Thus ends the training in the sequential integration.
